chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Zurara who said:
I saw upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) a saffron-dyed garment, and he said: Indeed I have married a woman from Quraysh.

key_terms.قُرَيْش: The noble Arab tribe of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), to which Imam al-Baqir himself belonged through his mother Umm Abdallah bint al-Hasan ibn Ali.
key_terms.مُعَصْفَر: Dyed with 'usfur (safflower/saffron); a yellow-orange dye. Wearing such garments was debated among jurists — this hadith supports their permissibility.

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Baqir wear saffron-dyed clothing?
ai.summary: Zurara, a trusted companion of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), narrates that he observed the Imam wearing saffron-dyed clothing. When the Imam noticed his attention, he explained that he had recently married a woman from the tribe of Quraysh. This hadith appears in the chapter on wearing dyed clothes and serves as evidence that such garments are permissible, particularly on occasions of marriage and celebration. In early Islamic culture, saffron-dyed ('mu'asfar') garments were associated with joyfulness and festivity.
